html:
The Salinan are a Native American people of the central coast of California, in the Salinas Valley and the Santa Lucia Mountains. The map spells the name Saunan.

They lived by gathering acorns and seeds, hunting and fishing, in small villages between the Ohlone to the north, the Chumash to the south and the Yokuts inland. Their language is not closely related to its neighbours.

Spain built two missions in their land: San Antonio de Padua in 1771 and San Miguel in 1797. Mission life and disease cut their numbers hard. Their descendants still live in the region and see themselves as a people. See also Salinan on the modern map.
sum: The Salinan are a Native American people of the central coast of California, in the Salinas Valley and the Santa Lucia Mountains. The map spells the name Saunan.
